title: Dominic and the Veil
premise: In the city of Corvane, where magic is punishable by unmaking, Yara Joubert survives by stealing memories and selling them as harmless charms. When a nameless child appears at his door speaking the First Tongue — the language that bound the kingdom's founding king to something ancient and hungry — Yara discovers the child carries a splinter of his own stolen past, and that the 'king' on the throne has been a vessel for the Veil for a decade. To free the realm, Yara must unbind a king who no longer exists, confront the memory-thief who taught him his trade and erased his childhood, and decide whether survival bought with stolen lives was ever worth the price. In the end, Yara gives back every memory he has ever taken — including his own — unbinding the Veil at the cost of knowing who he was, and the child, whole again, chooses to remember him.
about_author: Casper Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city and now writes about what people bury to stay alive. 'Dominic and the Veil' is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Yara Joubert lifts a dying soldier's last summer from his mind and sells it as a charm in Corvane's night market, establishing his trade, his rules, and the numbness that lets him survive. Third-person limited, Yara's POV. The beat is quiet complicity — a man who has made peace with a trade that should shame him.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: A child of six or seven appears at Yara's door speaking the First Tongue, a language that makes Yara's stolen memories ache and his charms crack. When the child touches him, Yara glimpses a crowned figure drowning in shadow. Yara's POV. The emotional beat is terror disguised as irritation — his carefully sealed life is already breaking.

chapters.title: What the Charms Remember
chapters.summary: Yara's inventory begins whispering in the child's voice, revealing that memories he stole over three years all contain fragments of the same dream: a king kneeling before a door in a hill. Yara's POV, with a brief interlude of the child's fragmented perception. The beat is dawning dread — he has been an unwitting courier of something enormous.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Wardens
chapters.summary: The Wardens — the crown's magic-hunters — raid the night market following traces of First Tongue resonance. Yara escapes with the child through the memory-thieves' tunnels, but his fence, Old Sefa, is taken. Yara's POV. The beat is the cost of sheltering the innocent: survival now requires allies he swore off.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Made Me
chapters.summary: Yara seeks his former master, Vess Corhane, the legendary memory-thief who erased Yara's childhood as payment for training. Vess recognizes the child's language and goes pale: she stole that memory herself, twenty years ago, from the king. Yara's POV. The beat is bitter reunion — the person who hollowed him is his only map.

chapters.title: The Door in the Hill
chapters.summary: Vess explains the Veil: a hunger older than kingdoms that the founding king bound beneath Corvane using the First Tongue, and which now wears the current king like a glove. The child is the binding's living key. Yara's POV. The beat is vertigo — the small crime of his life is a thread in a catastrophe centuries deep.

chapters.title: Court of Hollow Eyes
chapters.summary: Yara infiltrates the palace as a charm-seller to the court and sees the king up close: a man whose eyes reflect nothing, who speaks in perfect public warmth and private nothing. Yara witnesses the Veil feed on a servant's memory of her mother. Yara's POV. The beat is horror at power — corruption rendered as appetite.

chapters.title: The Price of the Child
chapters.summary: Wardens corner Yara and the child; to save him, Yara steals the memories of an entire Warden patrol, leaving them smiling blanks. The child watches and is frightened — of Yara, not the Wardens. Yara's POV. The beat is shame sharpened into a question: how is he different from the thing on the throne?

chapters.title: Vess's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vess reveals her ledger of every memory she has stolen in forty years, including the king's — and Yara's childhood, which she offers to return. Yara refuses, terrified of what he was. Vess's POV. The beat is tragic self-knowledge deferred: she has watched him choose numbness for three years and finally names it.

chapters.title: The Language of Doors
chapters.summary: The child begins teaching Yara the First Tongue, and speaking it returns stolen memories to their owners — including, painfully, fragments of Yara's own. He learns he was the child of memory-thieves the crown executed. Yara's POV. The beat is grief as inheritance: his emptiness was made, and can be unmade.

chapters.title: Sefa's Unmaking
chapters.summary: Yara finds Old Sefa in the Warden cells, half-unmade — her memories publicly burned as spectacle. She dies recognizing him and forgiving him for not coming sooner. Yara's POV. The beat is fury transmuted into resolve: the state's cruelty is not abstract anymore, and neither is his complicity in staying hidden.

chapters.title: The King Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Deep in the palace, Yara finds the real king — alive, memory-scoured, hidden beneath the throne — kept as the Veil's anchor. The king begs not for rescue but for oblivion to end. Yara's POV. The beat is moral vertigo: freeing the realm may mean granting a man the death he asks for.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Veil Speaks
chapters.summary: The Veil, wearing the king, confronts Yara directly and offers him everything: his childhood returned, his guilt dissolved, power over memory itself. For one suspended moment, Yara wants it. Yara's POV. The beat is the temptation of the theme made flesh — power as the promise that survival need never cost anything again.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Yara refuses; the Veil retaliates by unmaking the night market and everyone in it, and framing the memory-thieves for treason. Vess is captured. Yara escapes with the child into the hill country where the Door lies. Yara's POV. The beat is the collapse of every hiding place — there is no surviving this quietly.

chapters.title: The First Tongue, Spoken Whole
chapters.summary: In the ruins of a founding-era shrine, the child speaks the First Tongue fluently for the first time, and Yara understands: the child is not a key but a remnant — the founding king's erased humanity, given flesh. Yara's POV. The beat is awe and tenderness — the innocent he protected is the oldest wound in the kingdom.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Vess trades the location of the Door to the Veil in exchange for Yara's life — the same bargain she once refused to make for Yara's parents. Yara learns this from a stolen memory she smuggled out. Yara's POV. The beat is devastating love: her betrayal and her sacrifice are the same act.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Yara and the child enter the Door in the hill ahead of the Veil's Wardens, navigating a landscape built from the founding king's sealed memories — his love, his crimes, his original bargain with the hunger. Yara's POV. The beat is intimacy with the dead: the past is not a story but a place, and it is still occupied.

chapters.title: The Founding King's Confession
chapters.summary: At the binding's heart, the founding king's memory reveals the truth: he did not imprison the Veil — he fed it his people's memories to buy his crown, and the child is the one memory he could not bring himself to spend. Yara's POV. The beat is the theme laid bare: power was corruption from the first word of the spell.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: The Veil arrives wearing the king's body; Vess, freed or escaped, arrives bleeding to help. To unbind, every stolen memory must be returned — and Yara realizes the final payment is his own: everything he has taken, and everything taken from him. Yara's POV. The beat is the choice the whole book has aimed at.

chapters.title: Climax: Everything He Ever Took
chapters.summary: Yara speaks the unbinding in the First Tongue, pouring out three years of stolen memories and receiving his own childhood in a flood — his parents, his name, his grief — while the Veil, starved of what it wears, is forced out of the king and sealed by the child, who chooses to remain the binding's keeper. Yara's POV. The beat is agonizing release: he becomes whole exactly as he gives himself away.

chapters.title: The Empty Crown
chapters.summary: The real king, half-returned to himself, abdicates rather than rule a realm that fed on its own people; Corvane reels as the magic laws collapse and the unmade begin to be remembered. Yara, now carrying his full past, cannot bear the city. Yara's POV. The beat is aftermath — victory that feels like exile, and the question of what a survivor owes.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Him
chapters.summary: On the road out of Corvane, the child — the founding king's humanity, free now — catches up to Yara and speaks his true name, the one he lost at nine years old. Yara chooses to stay, to teach, to remember out loud. Yara's POV, closing with the child's voice. The beat is grace: identity is not what was stolen or returned, but what we choose to carry together.
